title: Dedicated: document autoscaling bounds + predictive mode (config, semantics, troubleshooting)
author: Elliot Price
release_notes: Docs: Added Dedicated autoscaling policy bounds (min/max) configuration guide + semantics and precedence.
Docs: Added Predictive Mode overview, when to use it, and safety/override behavior.
Docs: Added troubleshooting guidance for bound-hit saturation, queue buildup, and forecast staleness.
description: Summary This PR updates customer-facing documentation for Dedicated autoscaling policy bounds and Predictive Mode. It is written to support pilot->GA rollout and reduce support load by clarifying semantics (what is enforced, what is advisory), recommended starting ranges, and what to do when customers hit max bounds or experience queueing during ramps. The new docs cover: configuring min/max replicas (and GPU equivalent guidance), cooldown behavior, Predictive Mode basics, signal arbitration (reactive overrides predictions), and troubleshooting steps with references to the new dashboard panels/metrics. Motivation Recent Dedicated escalations (SUP-28411/SUP-28437) and pilot feedback indicated confusion around (1) whether max is a hard ceiling, (2) why scale-up may stop while queue grows, (3) how Predictive Mode interacts with reactive signals and cooldowns, and (4) what customers should do during region capacity shortages where min cannot be met. This PR consolidates answers into a single doc set and aligns wording with the ADR semantics (hard invariants: never exceed max, never drop below min; deterministic clamping; emit bounded-state signals). Scope / What changed - Added docs page: "Dedicated autoscaling policy" (min/max, cooldowns, predictive toggle, examples for common workloads) - Added section: "Predictive Mode" (what it is, required history, confidence, staleness, fallback to reactive) - Added "Recommended starting points" including baseline min for SLA protection and max as spend guardrail; includes guidance to iterate based on observed queue depth and bound-hit rate - Added troubleshooting playbook: "Max-bound saturation", "Oscillation/jitter", "Forecast stale/unavailable", "Min not met due to capacity shortage" with suggested mitigations and when to contact support - Updated API/Console configuration snippets and terminology to match implementation (field names and UI labels) - Added small FAQ (e.g., "Does Predictive Mode scale to zero?", "Can I exceed max during incidents?" -> no; use contract/CS process) Not in scope - No product behavior changes; this is documentation only - No full runbook content (SRE runbook lives in internal Confluence); we link to customer-facing troubleshooting steps and support contact points Testing - Docs site build + link check - Verified code snippets against Console API endpoint shapes referenced in ENG-22141 (as of 2025-08-21) Rollout notes - Docs are written to be feature-flag aware: clearly marked "Available by request during pilot" and "GA" sections. Where behavior differs between pilot builds and GA target (e.g., confidence indicator display), language is guarded to avoid overpromising. Screenshots are intentionally minimal; we rely on text that matches UX labels in DES-981 to avoid churn during final UI polish. Links - Linear: PM-1842, ENG-22149 - Support references: SUP-28501 (how to set bounds), SUP-28437 (daily ramp), SUP-28479 (oscillation) - Internal semantics: ADR "Autoscaling bounds precedence and safety invariants" (referenced but not linked in public docs) - Observability: references the public-facing metric names that appear in the Dedicated dashboard (bound hit rate, desired vs bounded replicas, queue depth) Changed areas/files (high-level) - docs/dedicated/autoscaling-policy.md (new) - docs/dedicated/predictive-mode.md (new) - docs/dedicated/troubleshooting/autoscaling.md (new) - docs/reference/api/dedicated-scaling-policy.md (updated) - docs/console/dedicated-scaling-policy-ui.md (updated) - docs/shared/glossary.md (updated terms: bound, desired, bounded desired, cooldown) - redirects + nav sidebar updates Example snippet added (from docs) JSON example: { "autoscaling_policy": { "min_replicas": 4, "max_replicas": 24, "cooldown_seconds": 180, "predictive_mode": "ENABLED" } } Notes: - The system will clamp requested desired replicas into [min_replicas, max_replicas]. - If predictive signal is stale/unavailable, the autoscaler falls back to reactive scaling (still respecting bounds).

docs(dedicated): add predictive mode overview + FAQ
docs(troubleshooting): add bounded scaling troubleshooting guide
docs(api): update dedicated scaling policy reference and field names
docs(nav): add Dedicated autoscaling section to sidebar + redirects
review_conversation: Kira Thompson (review): The bounds semantics section is close, but we need to explicitly state max is a hard ceiling and cannot be exceeded even during incident mitigation. Also add a short paragraph on what happens if customers set min > available regional capacity. Elliot Price (author): Updated: added "Hard invariants" callout (never exceed max; never drop below min) and a new "When min cannot be met" section explaining degraded state + retry and to contact support for capacity planning. Lauren Bishop (review): Please add a "Recommended starting points" section. Customers keep asking "what should my min be for SLA". It should be framed as guidance, not guarantees. Elliot Price (author): Added recommended ranges with disclaimers + a simple method: set min to cover typical baseline + ensure p95 during low traffic; set max as budget ceiling; iterate based on queue depth and bound-hit metrics. Included example values for steady workloads vs daily ramp workloads. Rafael Mendes (review): Troubleshooting needs to be careful not to tell customers to disable predictive mode without context; also include what to collect before opening a ticket (deployment_id, region, timeframe, bound-hit rate, queue depth). Elliot Price (author): Adjusted: added "Before contacting support" checklist and a decision tree: confirm bound saturation vs prediction staleness vs cooldown effects; disable predictive only if oscillation suspected and reactive scaling is stable. Allison Grant (review): Metric names: please use the exact public metric labels shown in Console dashboard (Desired Replicas, Bounded Desired Replicas, Max Bound Hit Rate, Queue Depth). Avoid adding internal Prometheus names into customer docs. Elliot Price (author): Done. Replaced internal metric identifiers with dashboard label names and added a note: "Your dashboard labels may vary slightly by region during pilot." Tessa Morgan (review): UX wording: Console uses "Predictive Mode" and a separate "Fallback to Reactive" toggle is not exposed; don't mention it as a customer setting. Also ensure validation messages match DES-981 (min/max errors). Elliot Price (author): Cleaned up: predictive fallback described as system behavior; removed references to a toggle. Updated validation examples to match current UI copy. Approvals: Kira Thompson approved, Lauren Bishop approved, Rafael Mendes approved after edits, Allison Grant approved, Tessa Morgan approved.
merge_outcome: Merged to main; published with next docs deploy window (2025-08-23 18:00 UTC).
